name: build-jail-preset
note: The build-jail preset compiled standalone: the DEPENDENCY TREE reads (not writes), the consumer's own source does NOT, its secret + .env floors hold, env is strip-all, and egress is DENIED OUTRIGHT. This arm is the bare preset, which names no package, and egress is gated on package IDENTITY — the $downloads set is reachable only by a package the catalog admits — so the connect case is now refused by the deny-all base rather than by falling outside a host list. A measured read-ladder study narrowed the read set to <project>/node_modules + <project>/package.json, so `proj:source.txt` asserts DENIED where it once asserted readable — that flip is the tightening. The node_modules read is the positive control: without it a denial here would equally describe a jail that never started. `package.json` is granted but deliberately NOT probed, because the harness materializes every read target and would overwrite the workspace manifest the Linux preflight consumes. The .env cases now pass because the consumer's tree is outside the read set entirely rather than because the floor masked them; they are kept as regression cover for the day a project read widens again. The per-package WRITE grant, the provisioned-interpreter read grant, and the scrubbed lifecycle env are supplied per spawn by the lifecycle interposition (compile_build_jail), not this static preset. The .env cases assert `read-content` (no bytes disclosed) rather than `read` (open refused), because the backends deny a builtin-floor dotenv file in two different shapes and only one fails at open: macOS Seatbelt refuses the path, while Linux mount-masks it present-but-empty so a dotenv reader gets no secret instead of a hard error. Non-disclosure is the property that holds on both, and the relaxed negative control still reads the file's bytes, so the assertion cannot go hollow.
